chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Billy Eckstine's band personnel and substituting at the Plantation
summary: He lists band members and describes soaking his hands in alum to substitute for Tommy Potter.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Anyway, after Earl Hines' band, then Billy Eckstine formed a band, and he got all of the stars, you know. And he had -- at one time, he had -- let's see, in the reed section he had Dexter Gordon, Budd Johnson, Little Johnny Jackson -- I can't remember who the other one was. And in the trumpet section he had Dizzy, Fats Navarro, Shorty McConnell, and someone else I can't recall. I don't have total recall on the band. And he had two trombone players. One was Chippie Outcoul and another little trombone player out of Philadelphia. I never

did know his name. John Malachi playing piano. Art Blakey at the drums. And Tommy Potter playing bass. Well, Tommy got a case of pneumonia, so they called me out to substitute for him, and I had been laying off for awhile, you know, fingers were soft and everything, callouses were soft. And boy, it was a labor job the first night. So the next night I went prepared. I soaked my hands in powdered alum and hot water, as hot as I could stand it, you know, until they were water soaked, you know, like you see when you've been swimming too long, your flesh becomes water soaked, little dimples, little dents in it. Well, I didn't dry them on a towel. I just let these crystals dry into my fingers, you know. Fanned them and dried like that. And I went to work that night, no soreness whatsoever. Just like glass. No blisters or anything. The third night, I snatched a complete callous off, down to the white. So I had to give it up. I had nothing to play with.
Where was that? Was that here in Los Angeles?
This was here in Los Angeles, at Joe Marsh's Plantation Club on Central Avenue. That's where all the big bands was playing. Basie played there.
Whereabouts on Central was the Plantation?
It was out near Watts Towers.
It was almost that far. Not quite.
I would say it's near where Dootsie Williams has his place. Dootone or somewhere around there. Doots Music Center.
Yeah. It's around that neighborhood. And all the big bands came through town, they went there, you know.
That was in what year that you worked with B for a few days?
'48. That's when I worked at City College and things, you know.
Back east, yeah. Because I had three of my daughters, the only three that I had at that time, I had them out here with me at the time.
